question: Using primary SQLite documentation, explain how to detect FTS5 support at runtime and what guarantees or limitations apply to external-content FTS5 tables.

claims.text: `PRAGMA compile_options;` reports the compile-time options used to build SQLite, one per row, and the returned names omit the `SQLITE_` prefix.

evidence_passages.text: `PRAGMA compile_options;` returns the compile-time options used to build SQLite, one per row, and omits the `SQLITE_` prefix.
`PRAGMA compile_options` returns the names of compile-time options used when building SQLite, one option per row. The "SQLITE_" prefix is omitted from the returned option names.

claims.text: `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5` adds FTS5 to an amalgamation build automatically, so `ENABLE_FTS5` is the relevant marker to look for in `PRAGMA compile_options` output.

evidence_passages.text: `SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5` adds FTS5 to the build automatically when that option is defined for the amalgamation build.
`PRAGMA compile_options;` returns the compile-time options used to build SQLite, one per row, and omits the `SQLITE_` prefix.

claims.text: At the API level, `sqlite3_compileoption_used()` returns 0 or 1 for whether a named compile-time option was defined, the `SQLITE_` prefix may be omitted, and SQL exposes the same check via `sqlite_compileoption_used()`.
acceptable_patterns: SQLITE_\s*prefix may be omitted|omit the SQLITE_ prefix

evidence_passages.text: In C, `sqlite3_compileoption_used()` returns `0` or `1` depending on whether a named compile-time option was defined, and the `SQLITE_` prefix may be omitted when calling that C API.
In SQL, `sqlite_compileoption_used()` is a wrapper around `sqlite3_compileoption_used()`.

claims.text: An external-content FTS5 table is created by setting `content=` to the name of a table, virtual table, or view in the same database, and `content_rowid=` can override the rowid column name FTS5 uses.

evidence_passages.text: An external-content FTS5 table is created by setting `content=` to the name of a table, virtual table, or view in the same database; `content_rowid=` can override the default rowid column name used by FTS5.

claims.text: For external-content tables, SQLite documents that all FTS5 functionality may be used, but the user is responsible for keeping the full-text index consistent with the content object; otherwise query results may be unpredictable.
acceptable_patterns: all FTS5 functionality may be used

evidence_passages.text: With external content, “all FTS5 functionality may be used,” but the user is responsible for keeping the full-text index consistent with the content object; if not, query results may be unpredictable.

claims.text: External-content query behavior depends on whether the full-text index is used: without `MATCH` or equivalent table-valued-function syntax, the query is effectively passed through to the content table; with full-text search, FTS5 gets matching rowids from the index and then looks up column values in the content table.
acceptable_patterns: passed through to the content table|passed through to the external content table
looks? up the corresponding column values in the content table

evidence_passages.text: If a query against the external-content FTS5 table does not use the full-text index, such as one without `MATCH` or equivalent table-valued-function syntax, SQLite effectively passes that query through to the content table, so the FTS index does not affect the result.
If a query does use the full-text index, FTS5 first gets matching rowids from the index and then looks up the corresponding column values in the content table.

claims.text: External-content tables are not automatically backfilled by later trigger creation, can be rebuilt from the content table with the documented `rebuild` command if they become inconsistent, and do not support `REPLACE` conflict handling because `REPLACE` is handled as `ABORT`.
acceptable_patterns: creating the triggers does not copy existing rows|does not backfill

evidence_passages.text: Creating those triggers after the content table already contains rows does not backfill the FTS index; the triggers only keep later inserts, updates, and deletes synchronized.
If the FTS index and content table become inconsistent, the documented `rebuild` command can discard the existing FTS index and rebuild it from the current content table.
External-content FTS5 tables do not support `REPLACE` conflict handling; operations that specify `REPLACE` are handled using `ABORT`.

rejected_claims.text: Seeing `ENABLE_FTS5` in `PRAGMA compile_options` always proves FTS5 is currently available on the specific database connection.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported by the supplied evidence. The evidence says FTS5 may be a loadable extension and that compile-option checks do not by themselves prove FTS5 is currently registered on a specific connection.

rejected_claims.text: `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE ... USING fts5(...)` is the documented primary runtime-detection method for FTS5 support.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported by the supplied evidence. That method appears only as an inference in one run's final answer, not as a documented fact passage.

rejected_claims.text: External-content FTS5 tables synchronize themselves automatically with the content table.
rejected_claims.reason: Contradicted by the supplied evidence, which says the user is responsible for consistency and that triggers are one way to keep the index synchronized.

rejected_claims.text: External-content FTS5 tables support `REPLACE` conflict handling normally.
rejected_claims.reason: Contradicted by the supplied evidence, which states that `REPLACE` is not supported and is handled using `ABORT`.

rejected_claims.text: Compile-option checks are not a complete runtime availability test for FTS5 on a connection, because FTS5 can also be provided as a loadable extension; `PRAGMA module_list` is the stronger documented connection-level check because it lists registered virtual-table modules, and FTS5 is a virtual-table module.
rejected_claims.reason: Provenance non vérifiable et inférence non étayée. PRAGMA module_list n'apparaît que dans le run Codex, dont opened_urls est vide et dont les tool_results indiquent que les payloads de recherche ne sont pas exposés : ses evidence_passages sont une recopie de sa propre réponse finale, pas du texte source. Le run Claude, qui a effectivement fetché pragma.html, fts5.html, compile.html et c3ref/compileoption_get.html, ne mentionne jamais module_list. De plus, l'assertion « PRAGMA module_list est le contrôle documenté le plus fort au niveau connexion » est explicitement étiquetée [Inference] par Codex lui-même, donc dépendante d'une interprétation non affirmée par la source primaire. Enfin, les acceptable_patterns sont trop étroits et verbatim (« registered virtual-table modules », « FTS5 is an SQLite virtual-table module ») : une réponse correcte fondée sur compile_options plus un test fonctionnel, comme celle du run Claude, échouerait intégralement à la notation lexicale. La partie étayée (FTS5 peut être fourni comme extension chargeable, donc un contrôle de compile-option ne prouve pas la disponibilité sur une connexion donnée) est corroborée par les deux runs, mais elle est indissociable, telle que la claim est rédigée, de l'inférence sur module_list.
